title: Fleet Cache Facts
description: 🛰️ The facts every machine of a fleet group needs to reach the group's cache without any per-machine step. The cache server of the group publishes them in the group store at <store>/v1/fleet/cache.json; every client resolves its remote cache contract from the environment first and from these facts second. The store is the trust boundary of the fleet (whoever mounts it already changes the code every machine runs), but the file carries no secret: every machine proves who it is with signed requests (see the identity schema), so a file that every member can read hands out no capability.

Endpoint.description: Origin of a cache server: http or https, host, optional port; no credentials, path, query or fragment.

Milliseconds.description: Wall clock time of the writing machine in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

Facts.description: The one fact file of a group, <store>/v1/fleet/cache.json. generation counts content changes and only grows. execution is reserved for the remote execution scheduler: it stays absent until a scheduler is published, and a client must ignore an absent execution.

publisher.description: The identity of the cache server that published these facts: its data directory, its listening port and its host name. A publisher with another identity never replaces recent facts and never lowers the generation, so a scratch or test server is detectable and harmless.

endpoints.description: Origins that reach the cache server from the workers, most preferred first; a client uses the first one that answers GET /healthz.

transport.description: How the machines of the group reach this server: `sealed` (every request travels inside the sealed exchange, see sealed/ schema) or `trusted-lan` (signed plain HTTP on a LAN the operator trusts). Absent means plain. Requests of other groups are always sealed.

auth.description: How clients prove who they are: signed requests of the origins (scheme semio-fleet-v1, see 🪪️identity). A client that does not know the scheme stays local.

execution.description: The remote execution scheduler of the group (reserved; absent until published).

LocalCopy.description: The machine's last known copy of the facts (<worktree>/.cache/f/cache-facts.json, mode 0600, never replicated): when it was fetched and which endpoint answered.
